title: Rivers (KS2)
subject: Geography
strapline: From source to mouth — the journey of a river.
facts: A river starts at its source, often high up in hills or mountains.
The place where a river ends and meets the sea is called the mouth.
A smaller river or stream that joins a bigger river is a tributary.
The mouth of a river is often where a wide, muddy estuary forms.
Rivers erode (wear away), transport (carry) and deposit (drop) material along their course.
People use rivers for drinking water, farming, transport, power and leisure.
The land a river flows through is called its valley; the sides are the banks.

quick_quiz.q: What is the start of a river called?
What do we call a smaller river that joins a bigger one?
Where does a river meet the sea?

teacher_tips: Trace a real river (e.g. the Thames) from source to mouth on a map.
Model erosion and deposition in a sand tray with poured water.
Use the key vocabulary (source, tributary, mouth) as labels on a diagram.
